metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–15% for 3–5 subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance and anchor to recent 7-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 14-day high, reduce by 2–4% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after spike, model often fails to recognize it — add a 3–5 day lagged decay factor to forecast tail.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extrapolating from 18-day history; use 30-day rolling mean as baseline for correction if sentiment is flat.
